learningObjective: Distinguish the roles of Operation, Region, Block, Value, Type, and Attribute in the MLIR structural model, and identify which entity carries compile-time constants vs. SSA runtime values.

canonicalClaims.claim: In MLIR, an Operation may contain zero or more Regions, each Region contains one or more Blocks (Block list), Blocks contain Operations recursively; SSA Values are produced and consumed by Operations at runtime, while Attributes are compile-time constant metadata attached to an Operation.
conditions: The IR follows the MLIR structural model documented in LangRef.
Attribute values are not mutated during execution.
nonImplications: Does not imply every Op has Regions; leaf Ops (arith.addi) have zero Regions.
Does not imply Regions are always SSACFG; Graph regions also exist.

sourceMappings.locator: Operations, Regions, Blocks, Values, Types, Attributes

misconceptions.claim: Attributes are SSA runtime values attached to Ops.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Attributes are compile-time constants on Ops; SSA Values are Operation operands/results.

misconceptions.claim: Blocks are the top-level unit of MLIR IR; each Block owns exactly one Region.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The top-level unit is an Operation (typically ModuleOp) containing a Region containing Blocks; Blocks do not own Regions.

misconceptions.claim: Every Value in MLIR must carry its own Attribute alongside its Type.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Values have Types only; Attributes are attached to Ops.

misconceptions.claim: A Region in MLIR is limited to a single Block.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Regions may contain multiple Blocks forming a CFG; single-block regions are just a common special case.

implementationFacts: ModuleOp: an Operation with a single Region containing one Block of top-level Ops.
arith.constant carries a `value` Attribute and produces one SSA Value of a given Type.
